name: Unicorn Outcome and Valuation Label Guardrail

positioning.oneLineSummary: Prevents a billion-dollar headline valuation or unicorn-pattern match from being presented as economic value, fund return, or an investment decision.
positioning.productLabel: Outcome-Label Guardrail — based on Super Founders scope with share-class valuation evidence
notAClaimOf: a replacement for valuation or waterfall models

attribution.display: Based on the Super Founders billion-dollar-valuation outcome definition and external share-class valuation research

neutralParaphrase: Super Founders studies whether companies reached a billion-dollar private valuation. That label can be useful for studying an extreme financing outcome, but it is not the same as company enterprise value, common-share fair value, a specific security's payoff, realized investor return, or current investment attractiveness. The runtime must display the label, terms, ownership, dilution, scenarios, and valuation outputs separately.

locator.value: Official title, description, and study target: billion-dollar startup valuations
Study design: companies with billion-dollar valuations versus selected non-unicorn comparison group
Abstract and published-version metadata: share-class rights and overstatement in headline post-money valuations

requiredConditions: The analysis distinguishes research label, financing headline, security value, and realized return.
Current round documents and fully diluted ownership are available before making price claims.
All numeric calculations are delegated to deterministic valuation, cap-table, and waterfall services.

requiredEvidence.description: Price per share, invested amount, pre- and post-money convention, liquidation preferences, seniority, participation, conversion, guarantees, vetoes, and other economic rights.
All issued, reserved, promised, convertible, and option securities by class and holder.
Bear, base, and bull operating assumptions and enterprise or equity values with sensitivity.
Investor ownership after dilution and payoff by security under exit scenarios.
Whether the value is last-round mark, model mark, tender price, acquisition proceeds, IPO value, or distributed cash.

decisionQuestions: What exactly does the billion-dollar figure value and under which convention?
Which share class established the price and what protections does it have?
What is the value of the security being considered under each scenario?
How do dilution, preferences, and future capital change investor payoff?
Is the observed outcome a mark, liquidity event, or distributed cash?
Would the company still be attractive at the requested terms without the unicorn label?
positiveSignals: Headline and security-specific values are clearly separated.
All security terms and fully diluted ownership are modeled.
Bear, base, and bull payoffs can be independently recomputed.
The company thesis remains credible without the unicorn label.
Realized and unrealized outcomes are displayed separately.
redFlags: Last preferred price is multiplied by all shares without rights adjustment.
Unicorn status is used as proof of intrinsic value or future return.
Common and preferred interests are treated as identical.
A financing announcement substitutes for current operating valuation.
Pattern match to prior unicorns produces an investment recommendation.
disconfirmingEvidence: Preferences or guarantees create materially different class values.
A realistic downside waterfall gives the target security little or no return.
Future financing materially dilutes ownership or adds senior claims.
The round price implies operating assumptions unsupported by evidence.
A reported mark has no arm's-length liquidity.
contraindications: Do not use this card as a valuation calculator.
Do not output Invest Candidate from a unicorn pattern match.
Do not equate private post-money, fair value, enterprise value, common value, and realized proceeds.
Do not make legal or tax conclusions.

instructions: Label every value by date, convention, share class, and realization status.
Send cap-table, valuation, and waterfall calculations to deterministic services.
Compare requested terms with security-specific bear, base, and bull payoffs.
Keep Super Founders pattern observations in a separate descriptive section.
Conclude only on label integrity and missing valuation evidence.

deterministicRule.calculationOwner: Valuation, Cap Table, Waterfall, and Fund Model services

sourceReliability.low: Only press valuations or founder claims are available.
sourceReliability.medium: Official financing announcements and partial terms are available.
sourceReliability.high: Executed documents, cap table, audited records, and model inputs are reviewed.

evidenceStrength.medium: Round price and some terms exist but class rights or scenarios are incomplete.
evidenceStrength.high: Terms, cap table, operating evidence, valuation, dilution, and waterfall converge.

evidenceCoverage.low: Share-class rights or cap table is missing.
evidenceCoverage.medium: Current round is modeled but future dilution or realization status is incomplete.
evidenceCoverage.high: All classes, terms, scenarios, dilution, payoff, and realization states are covered.

applicabilityConfidence.low: No billion-dollar or financing valuation claim is material.
applicabilityConfidence.medium: A headline valuation exists but is not central to the decision.
applicabilityConfidence.high: The investment thesis or report relies materially on unicorn status or round price.

judgmentConfidence.low: The system cannot distinguish labels and economic value.
judgmentConfidence.medium: The label is qualified but some deterministic inputs are missing.
judgmentConfidence.high: Every value is correctly scoped and recomputable from reviewed inputs.

promotionRequirements: Integrate verified deterministic valuation, cap-table, and waterfall services.
Review transaction-specific legal documents and current valuation policy.
Validate label-integrity checks on historical financing events.
empiricalQualifications: Private post-money values can overstate economic value when share classes have different rights.
The source study's outcome is a financing valuation, not risk-adjusted or realized return.
Security-specific value depends on terms and scenarios.

rights.notes: No book or academic paper passage is reproduced.

openIssues: Complete transaction-law and deterministic-service integration review.

changeLog.summary: Initial outcome-label guardrail separating unicorn status from economic value.
